key_insight: A two-layer quantum circuit can encode a long matrix-chain product in depth that stays independent of chain length K, trading qubits and linear total gates for much lower depth.
engineering_relevance: This is useful when matrix-chain products must be embedded as statevector subroutines in quantum workflows such as kernel methods, linear solvers, graph routines, and norm estimation.
method: Interleave state-preparation operators across two towers so operators in each layer act on disjoint registers in parallel.
Use a QRAM-based state-preparation model to represent the product of K matrices as a quantum state.
Specialize the construction to the chain-vector case for multiplying a matrix chain by a vector.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a correctness proof for all K and two implementations in Qiskit and QCLAB, but does not describe empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The depth advantage depends on QRAM-based state preparation, while qubit count grows as the sum of log dimensions and total gate count still scales linearly with K.
paper_title: Two-Tower Quantum Matrix Chain Multiplication: Trading Qubits for Depth
